headline: Seventeen countries led by the United States have endorsed a Kyoto declaration on using AI in science, but it carries no money or binding commitments.
score_reason: Lowered from 6: the declaration came out on 4 Oct, before the window; what is new is the final list of 17 countries and its non-binding wording.
importance_line: Scientists in the 17 countries get a shared statement that AI-run labs and wider access to data and computing are goals for research policy, but the text commits no money, sets no targets and has no enforcement, and China and India are not signatories.
summary: Tech Times reports that the United States and 16 other countries endorsed the Kyoto Vision declaration on 4 Oct 2026 at the annual Science and Technology in Society Forum in Kyoto, urging that AI, which the text calls 'super intelligence', be built into scientific research, but that no signatory pledged money, signed a treaty or accepted any enforcement. This follows NBC News's 3 Oct report, carried in our 4 Oct edition, that the United States and 15 other countries would release it; new today are the final list of 17 countries, without China or India, and Tech Times's point that the White House's words 'pledged' and 'committed' do not appear in the declaration.
notes: The AI News original was behind a captcha, so the same story was read on Tech Times (the source credited here) and News9live (same list of countries and the same 'no binding targets or budgets' finding), plus NBC News's 3 Oct advance report. Continues item 58 of our 4 Oct edition (NBC News, score 7). Tech Times includes its own commentary, which is left out. Score lowered by one because the release happened on 4 Oct, before the window.
